html:
Bolsa Família (Family Allowance) is the main welfare programme of Brazil, created in 2003 under President Lula da Silva. It pays small monthly sums to poor families, usually to the mother, on condition that the children go to school and get their vaccinations and health checks.

It merged several older grants into one and became part of Lula's Fome Zero (Zero Hunger) drive. At its height it reached about a quarter of Brazil's people, yet it cost only a small share of the federal budget. Economists credit it with a real part of the fall in poverty and inequality in Brazil in the 2000s.

The idea of paying cash with conditions, a conditional cash transfer, was pioneered by Mexico's Progresa in 1997. Bolsa Família made it famous. The World Bank promoted it, and dozens of countries in Latin America, Africa and Asia built similar schemes. President Jair Bolsonaro replaced it with Auxílio Brasil in 2021; Lula brought back the old name in 2023.
